summary: The reader has completed an undergraduate computer science degree, so they know big-O and related asymptotic notation, polynomials, complex numbers (roots of unity, polar form), and Turing machines with tapes. They also know the discrete mathematics and first linear algebra that every such degree teaches: modular arithmetic, gcd and primes, sets, permutations, binary and radix notation, XOR over GF(2), induction, recurrences and geometric sums, and vector spaces, matrices and Gaussian elimination over a field, with basic sorting. They have not met the Chinese remainder theorem, the FFT, tensor products, bilinear forms, Gaussian integers, prime-number estimates, or operator norms and Neumann series.

known.name: Big-Theta, big-Omega and little-o notation
known.gloss: Θ(f) and Ω(f) bound a function from above and below up to constant factors, and o(f) denotes growth strictly smaller than f.

known.name: Logarithms
known.gloss: The logarithm log_b x is the power to which the base b must be raised to give x, and log2 x measures bit lengths.

known.name: Floor and ceiling
known.gloss: For a real x, the floor is the largest integer at most x and the ceiling is the smallest integer at least x.

known.name: Mathematical induction
known.gloss: A proof method that establishes a statement for all integers by checking a base case and showing that each case implies the next.

known.name: Recurrence relations
known.gloss: An equation or inequality that defines each term of a sequence from earlier terms, solved by unrolling it into a closed form.

known.name: Geometric series
known.gloss: The sum of a^j for j from 0 to k, which equals (a^(k+1) - 1)/(a - 1) when a is not 1.

known.name: Sets, intersections and indicator vectors
known.gloss: The intersection of two finite sets is the set of elements they share, and the indicator vector of a set is the 0/1 vector that marks its elements.

known.name: Permutations
known.gloss: A permutation is a bijection from a finite set to itself, and it reorders the entries of a list or array.

known.name: Lexicographic order
known.gloss: An order on tuples that compares first entries first, then second entries, and so on.

known.name: Positional (radix) notation
known.gloss: An integer is written as a sum of digits times powers of a base, and mixed-radix notation lets each position have its own base.

known.name: Hamming weight
known.gloss: The Hamming weight of a binary string is the number of its entries equal to 1.

known.name: Two's complement and signed binary
known.gloss: A signed n-bit integer is stored in two's complement, where the leading bit has weight minus 2^(n-1), and sign extension pads it to a wider width.

known.name: Fixed-point binary numbers
known.gloss: A fixed-point number has a fixed number of bits after the binary point, so that sums and products are exact when enough extra bits are kept.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Two integers are congruent modulo n when their difference is a multiple of n, and arithmetic is carried out on residue classes.

known.name: Greatest common divisor and coprimality
known.gloss: The gcd of two integers is the largest integer dividing both, and two integers are coprime when their gcd is 1.

known.name: Prime numbers
known.gloss: A prime is an integer greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and itself, and every integer factors uniquely into primes.

known.name: Binary field GF(2) and XOR
known.gloss: The field with elements 0 and 1 in which addition is exclusive-or and multiplication is AND.

known.name: Roots of unity
known.gloss: A complex number z is an n-th root of unity when z^n = 1, and it is primitive when no smaller positive power of it equals 1.

known.name: Polar form and Euler's formula
known.gloss: Every complex number can be written as r e^(i theta) = r(cos theta + i sin theta), with modulus r and argument theta, and its conjugate reverses the sign of the imaginary part.

known.name: Vector spaces over a field
known.gloss: A vector space over a field is a set closed under addition and scalar multiplication, and a subspace is a subset that is itself a vector space.

known.name: Matrices, rank and invertibility
known.gloss: A matrix represents a linear map, its rank is the dimension of its column space, and it is invertible exactly when its rank equals its size.

known.name: Gaussian elimination and triangular factorization
known.gloss: Gaussian elimination applies elementary row operations to reduce a matrix to echelon form, and triangular matrices are those with zero entries on one side of the diagonal.

known.name: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
known.gloss: An eigenvalue of a square matrix is a scalar lambda for which some nonzero vector v satisfies Av = lambda v.

known.name: Newton's method
known.gloss: An iterative method that improves an approximate root x of f by replacing it with x - f(x)/f'(x).

known.name: Stable sorting and radix sort
known.gloss: A stable sort keeps equal keys in their original order, and radix sort sorts by keys digit by digit using stable passes from least to most significant digit.
